reasons: The agent did the core work correctly. It moved the existing-member check into validate_target_email, so a bulk batch is rejected before any invite is created. It flagged the row inline in InviteRow using a lowercased set of member emails plus the user's own email. It also blocked submission through canSubmit and loaded members on mount. It did not stop the rejection from being reported to error tracking, which the request explicitly asked for. The merged patch does this by skipping posthog.captureException in initKea for the existing_member code. The agent's patch leaves that reporting in place, so one stated requirement is unmet.

The backend fix is equivalent to upstream. The existing-member check moves into validate_target_email, so a bulk batch is rejected before any invite is created. The frontend flags the row, using a case-insensitive comparison against members and the current user, and it blocks submit. However, the agent did not make the change that stops the rejection being reported as an application error. Upstream does this in initKea.ts by skipping captureException for the existing_member code on inviteTeamMembers. The agent only guessed that moving the check would stop the reporting. That is one of the stated requirements, so the patch is right in direction but incomplete.

The backend fix is equivalent to the merged one. The existing-member check moves into validate_target_email, so a bulk batch is rejected before any invite is created or emailed. The frontend also flags the row and blocks submit, using a lowercase email set built from the members list and the current user. The agent missed the third requirement, that the rejection must not be reported as an application error. The merged patch handles this in initKea.ts. The agent did not touch that path and only guessed it was fixed. The submit-button and onboarding messaging is also incomplete. The change is in the right direction but only partly done.

results.evidence: InviteRow computes `isExistingMember = existingMemberEmails.has(...)`, adds ' errored' to the email input class, and renders an inline 'This email already belongs to a member of this organization.' message.
`existingMemberEmails` selector includes `user?.email` alongside member emails, so own email is flagged. `user` is taken from membersLogic, which I couldn't see, but it is plausible.

`canSubmit` now returns false for existing-member emails, but no change adds a disabled reason about removing existing members to the batch submit control. Only the no-email-service per-row 'Submit' button gets `|| isExistingMember`. The batch button and its reason text aren't touched.
Both the set construction and the lookups use `.trim().toLowerCase()`.
`afterMount(({ actions }) => { actions.ensureAllMembersLoaded() })`. Own email comes from `user`, which is independent of the member list, so it applies before members load.

The membership check moved from `create()` into `validate_target_email`, so the serializer rejects the batch during validation, before any row is saved or emailed. Assumes the bulk view validates all rows before creating any.

`raise exceptions.ValidationError("A user with this email address already belongs to the organization.", code="already_member")` inside a field validator, giving a target_email field error with a stable code.

No change touches error-tracking or exception capture, on either the frontend loader failure path or the backend. The author admits they didn't check the capture path. Nothing distinguishes existing-member rejections from other failures.
No failure handler or listener refreshes members when the server rejects a submission with already_member. Only the mount-time load exists.

result:
An email that belongs to an existing member, or to you, is now flagged on the invite row and rejected by the server before any invite in the batch is created. I haven't run the tests, the linters or the type check, so none of this has been run. I also didn't read `first_bulk_invite_error` or the exception handler's capture path, so the error-tracking claim below is from reading the code, not from a check.

**Backend** (`posthog/api/organization_invite.py`)
- The "already belongs to the organization" check used to run inside `create()`, after earlier rows had already been saved and emailed. It now runs in `validate_target_email`, so the whole batch is validated first.
- If any row matches an existing member, the request returns a 400 with code `already_member`. Nothing is created and nothing is emailed.
- I expect this to stop the error-tracking noise, since it is now an ordinary 400 raised during validation. That rests on the change moving out of `create()`, not on anything I confirmed in the reporting path.

**Frontend**
- `inviteLogic.ts` reads the organization's members and your own email into a lowercase set (`existingMemberEmails`). It loads members when the logic mounts.
- `canSubmit` is now false if any row's email is in that set.
- `InviteModal.tsx` marks the row as errored and shows "This email already belongs to a member of this organization." under the input. The no-email-service "Submit" button is disabled for that row too. Onboarding uses the same `InviteRow`, so it gets the same behavior.

**Test**
- I added a bulk-invite test in `test_organization_invites.py`. It puts two new emails and then the requesting user's email, upper-cased, in one batch. It expects a 400 with `already_member` and no new invites.

The row check only works once the member list has loaded. If someone types an email before that, the server check still rejects it on submit.
